newsitem.title: USA: Argentine wheat makes inroads beyond Latam - attache.
newsitem.headline: Argentine wheat makes inroads beyond Latam - attache.

text.p: Faced with an expected near-record wheat crop, Argentine exporters have mounted an aggressive wheat marketing program and made inroads in new markets outside Latin America, a U.S. agriculture attache said.

In a report dated Nov. 20 drafted in Buenos Aires, the attache said Argentina had already sold a reported 4.04 million tonnes of wheat, compared with 2.4 million tonnes in the same period last year. This represents about 40 percent of the total expected exports for this year, the attache said.
U.S. Agriculture Department has forecast Argentina's 1996/97 wheat crop at 14.5 million tonnes and exports at 10 million tonnes.

The attache said although Brazil was expected to take the lion's share of Argentine wheat exports, other markets, notably north African and eastern European markets, were also expected to be important, with large sales already made.

The attache cited Algeria, Egypt, Bulgaria, Malaysia, Poland, Sudan and Turkey as examples of countries where Argentine wheat had made inroads, or sales were expected to increase over historical levels.
"With a significant quantity of Argentine wheat yet to be priced in the market, we expect to see continued sales outside the Latin American region at competitive prices," he wrote.
